audit.whatIsWrong: The content win[] array reads Gwen / Skill / Rumble / Rumble / Gwen / Rumble / Rumble, which disagrees with its own whys at almost every stage and with the mirror audit at audits/top/rumble__gwen.json.
audit.why: whys[0] and whys[1] both describe Rumble winning levels 1-2, whys[3] says Hallowed Mist plus Needlework flips it, whys[4] hands level 6 back to him on Equalizer, whys[5] says 'even window', and whys[6] gives Gwen the isolated late duel. The mirror already settled the same array: Rumble / Rumble / Rumble / Gwen / Rumble / Skill / Gwen.
audit.corrected: win[] set to the mirror's array so the two directions agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon is described only as a slow. It also reduces MAGIC RESIST, he carries two harpoons, and the shred stacks — the mirror flags this as the largest damage lever in the lane and it is absent from Gwen's side too.
audit.why: Rumble's whole kit is magic damage. Leading with two harpoons cuts your MR before the Flamespitter lands, which is why an E-E-Q rotation hurts so much more than the page implies — and why the harpoons, not the cone, are what you must not eat for free.
audit.corrected: Stated in whys[1], the level 1-3 spike, wants.foe[1] and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Engage right after he empties his heat bar' is the page's key read and it never says what actually happens at 100% heat, nor gives any cooldown.
audit.why: Riot's text: at 100% Heat he starts Overheating, gains attack speed and bonus auto damage, and is UNABLE TO CAST SPELLS for a few seconds. That is the concrete window — no Flamespitter, no Equalizer, no harpoons — with the trade-off that his autos hit harder. Flamespitter is 10s at rank 1, Scrap Shield a flat 6s, and The Equalizer 130/105/80s.
audit.corrected: The Overheat cast-lock stated, plus cooldowns in the whys, mid and cooldown breakdown.

edits.before: Electro Harpoon (E) slows you so you can't leave the Flamespitter, and Overheat autos chunk you before you spike.
edits.after: Two Electro Harpoons stack a MAGIC RESIST cut on you before the cone even lands, and you cannot walk out of the slow.

edits.before: Catch him right after his heat bar empties, when Flamespitter damage and his Overheat autos drop off
edits.after: Close while he is Overheating at 100% heat — he cannot cast a single spell for those seconds

edits.before: Land Electro Harpoon (E) to slow you, then channel a full Flamespitter rotation before you reach mist range
edits.after: Land both Electro Harpoons to shred your Magic Resist and slow you, then channel a full Flamespitter

edits.before: Rumble's Flamespitter (Q) is free heat-fueled DPS that out-chips your melee form, and his Electro Harpoon (E) slows you so you can't walk out of the cone.
edits.after: Flamespitter (Q, 10s) is free heat-fuelled DPS, and his two Electro Harpoons slow you AND stack a Magic Resist cut so the cone lands far harder.

edits.before: Rumble owns levels 1-3. His Flamespitter (Q) is a wall of heat-fueled magic damage that melts your melee form, and you have no Hallowed Mist and no Skip 'n Slash reset to escape the cone yet — and his Electro Harpoon (E) slows you so you can't even back out of it. Don't try to trade into a full Flamespitter; if you step up he just chunks you with Overheat-empowered autos (no, he can't silence you, but the burst is real) and shoves you off the wave. Last-hit at the edge of his Q range, accept the chip, and never let him land E plus a full Flamespitter channel on you at once.
edits.after: Rumble owns levels 1-3. Flamespitter (Q, 10s) is a wall of heat-fuelled magic damage that melts your melee form, and you have no Hallowed Mist and no Skip 'n Slash reset to escape the cone. Worse, he carries TWO Electro Harpoons and each one cuts your Magic Resist as well as slowing you, so an E-E into a full channel is the real combo — not the cone on its own. Last-hit at the edge of his Q range, accept the chip, and never eat both harpoons and a full Flamespitter in the same window. If he steps up with heat banked he chunks you with Overheat-empowered autos and shoves you off the wave — give up the CS, not the health bar.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still his — you're a fog-less melee eating poke — but Level 6 is your flip. Once you have Needlework (R) plus Hallowed Mist (W), drop your fog on yourself before you commit: anything outside the cloud can't target you, so his single-target poke goes dead while you slow him with R and E in for the attack-speed and on-hit range. The one trap: his Equalizer is ground AOE that burns you even inside your mist, so place your fog to the SIDE of the burn, not on top of it. The key read is his heat bar — engage right after he empties it, when Flamespitter is weak and his autos lose the Overheat bonus.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your flip. Once you have Needlework (R) plus Hallowed Mist (W), drop your fog before you commit: anything outside the cloud cannot target you, so his poke goes dead while you slow him with R and E in for the attack speed and on-hit range. The trap: Equalizer is ground AoE that burns you inside the mist, so place your fog to the SIDE of the burn. The key read is his heat bar — at 100% he Overheats and cannot cast ANY spell for a few seconds, so that is when you close, even though his autos hit harder. Engage on the empty bar, not on the cone, and keep Skip 'n Slash for the reset rather than the escape.

edits.before: Track Rumble's Scrap Shield: Bait it, then commit. When it is down — Snip him in your mist.
edits.after: Two Electro Harpoons stack a MAGIC RESIST cut — E-E is the real combo, not the cone.

edits.before: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — Bait it, then commit. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Overheat at 100% heat: he cannot cast for a few seconds — your commit window. - Flamespitter (Q): 10s at rank 1. - Scrap Shield: a flat 6s. - The Equalizer: 130/105/80s of ground burn your mist does not stop.
